interface.signature: def longestSubstring(N: int, S: str) -> str:

preconditions.description: The length of the string S is between 1 and 1000.
The input S is a string.

postconditions.description: The function returns either '-1' or a non-empty string.
If a non-overlapping repeating substring exists, it is returned and appears at least twice in S without overlapping.

postconditions.expression: all(S[i:i+len(return_value)] != S[j:j+len(return_value)] for i in range(len(S)) for j in range(i+1, len(S)-len(return_value)+1) if i != j and S[i:i+len(return_value)] == S[j:j+len(return_value)])
postconditions.description: The returned substring does not overlap with any other occurrence of itself in S.

postconditions.expression: all(len(sub) < len(return_value) for sub in {S[i:j] for i in range(len(S)) for j in range(i+1, len(S)+1) if S.count(S[i:j]) >= 2 and S.find(S[i:j]) != S.rfind(S[i:j])}) or return_value == '-1'
postconditions.description: The returned substring is the longest non-overlapping repeating substring in S, or '-1' if none exists.
